summary: An Arabic typeface in regular and bold with simple, fairly even naskh-style letters. It works well for everyday Arabic text.
history: The font's copyright notice says it was designed by the Al Bayan Company for Computer Services, with Apple copyright dates of 1992–1998. That puts it in the classic Mac OS era. It is one of Apple's longest-serving Arabic fonts and was among the seven Arabic fonts that shipped with OS X 10.8.
designers: Al Bayan Company for Computer Services

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with macOS Sequoia

summary: A traditional naskh-style Arabic typeface in regular and bold, with graceful contrast between thick and thin strokes. A good choice for readable Arabic body text.
history: Al Nile carries a 1993 copyright from Diwan Science and Information Technology, the original name of the Arabic publishing-software company Diwan, which was founded in 1985. Apple added it to the Mac in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013), along with several other Diwan Arabic fonts.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A single-weight Arabic typeface in a classic, lightly calligraphic naskh style. Suited to headings and short texts with a traditional feel.
history: Al Tarikh was made by Diwan Software (2001 copyright). Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013), when Mac OS X gained about a dozen new Arabic-script fonts.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A clean, modern Korean sans serif (gothic) typeface in nine weights, from Thin to Heavy. It is Apple's standard Korean font for interfaces and body text.
history: Apple SD Gothic Neo was made by the Seoul foundry Sandoll for Apple. It is based on Sandoll's own Gothic Neo1 superfamily. Sandoll dates the project to 2011 and describes it as the default Korean system font on all Apple devices. It covers all 11,172 modern Hangul syllables plus a large set of Chinese characters (hanja).

summary: An older Korean gothic (sans serif) typeface from Apple, with plain, even strokes and a simple Latin alphabet. Useful for compatibility with older Korean Mac documents.
history: AppleGothic is one of Apple's own Korean fonts, with copyright dates of 1994–2006. Wikipedia's list of CJK fonts notes that it has fully supported Unicode Hangul since Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard. It has since been superseded by Apple SD Gothic Neo.

summary: A Korean serif typeface in the myeongjo (Ming) style, with brush-derived strokes, wedge-shaped terminals, and a matching serif Latin. Good for traditional-looking Korean text.
history: AppleMyungjo is one of Apple's own Korean fonts, with copyright dates of 1994–2007. Wikipedia's list of CJK fonts notes that it has fully supported Unicode Hangul since Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard.

summary: A sans serif Hebrew typeface that pairs with Arial, in Light, Regular, and Bold. It includes vowel points (niqqud) and cantillation marks.
history: Arial Hebrew is one of the Monotype versions of Arial made for other scripts, and Monotype also sells it separately. Its data carries 1990–1993 copyrights from Monotype and Type Solutions. Since OS X 10.9 Mavericks, Apple ships its weights together in a single ArialHB font collection.

summary: A companion version of Arial Hebrew in the same three weights, intended for texts that use full vowel pointing and cantillation marks.
history: Arial Hebrew Scholar comes in the same Apple font file as Arial Hebrew and carries the same 1990–1993 Monotype and Type Solutions copyright. Both fonts cover the same Hebrew characters. Apple does not publicly document how the Scholar version differs.

summary: A Thai typeface with plain, looped letterforms and fixed-width (monospaced) Latin characters. This gives it a tidy, typewriter-like rhythm.
history: Ayuthaya is one of Apple's own Thai fonts, with copyright dates of 1992–2011. It has shipped with Mac OS X alongside Apple's other Thai fonts, such as Krungthep, Sathu, Silom, and Thonburi.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A single-weight Arabic typeface with simple, low-contrast naskh-style letters, suited to general Arabic text.
history: According to its copyright notice, Baghdad was designed by Diwan Software, with Apple copyright dates of 1992–1998. It was one of the seven Arabic fonts that shipped with OS X 10.8 and is still included with macOS.

summary: A Bengali (Bangla) typeface in regular and bold, with moderately contrasted strokes and a humanist Latin companion. Suitable for Bengali and Assamese text.
history: Bangla MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2009 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "MN" family of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts. Fonts In Use notes that the plain MN fonts pair the script with a humanist sans Latin that has some stroke contrast.

summary: A Bengali (Bangla) typeface in regular and bold, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. It gives Bengali text a clean, modern look.
history: Bangla Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2003 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A very heavy, compact Arabic display typeface with bold, blocky strokes. It works best for headlines and short, punchy text.
history: Beirut was made by Diwan Software (2001 copyright). Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013), when Mac OS X gained about a dozen new Arabic-script fonts.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A slanted, cursive-flavored Hebrew typeface in regular and bold that gives Hebrew text a flowing, handwritten feel. Good for invitations and display use.
history: Corsiva Hebrew is a Monotype design. Its data carries 1990–1993 copyrights from Monotype and Type Solutions, and "Corsiva" is a Monotype trademark. Since OS X 10.9 Mavericks, Apple has shipped its regular and bold styles in a single font collection.

summary: A clean, contemporary Arabic typeface in five weights, with simple, even strokes. A versatile choice for Arabic text and interfaces.
history: Damascus comes from Diwan Software, with copyright dates of 1987–2012. It was one of the seven Arabic fonts in OS X 10.8, and Diwan also sells it commercially through MyFonts.

summary: A richly traditional Arabic typeface modeled on classical naskh calligraphy, with many ligatures and pen-shaped strokes. It suits literary and religious texts that call for an authentic calligraphic look.
history: DecoType Naskh was created by Thomas Milo of DecoType, a firm known for calligraphy-based Arabic type technology. The font carries 1992–2007 DecoType copyrights. It was one of the seven Arabic fonts that shipped with OS X 10.8 and is still included with macOS.

summary: A traditional Devanagari typeface in regular and bold, with calligraphic contrast and a serif Latin companion. Suitable for Hindi, Marathi, Sanskrit, and other languages written in Devanagari.
history: Devanagari MT is a Monotype design with a 1996 copyright. The name inside the font file is "Monotype Devanagari".

summary: A Devanagari typeface in regular and bold, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. It gives Hindi and Marathi text a clean, modern look.
history: Devanagari Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2003 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A geometric Arabic display typeface in the angular Kufic style, with straight strokes and squared-off forms. Best for titles, logos, and decorative use.
history: Diwan Kufi was made by Diwan Software (2001 copyright). Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013). Kufic is the oldest style of Arabic calligraphy and is still widely used in architecture and decoration.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: An ornate Arabic typeface in the Thuluth calligraphic style, with tall, sweeping letters that stack and overlap. Made for formal headings and decorative text.
history: Diwan Thuluth was made by Diwan Software (2001 copyright); its font notice says it was programmed by Anmar Sabeeh and Abu Hassan. Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013).
designers: Diwan Software Ltd. (programmed by Anmar Sabeeh & Abu Hassan)

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A humanist sans serif typeface for Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics, with a matching Latin alphabet. It covers languages such as Cree, Inuktitut, and Carrier.
history: Euphemia was designed by Ross Mills of Tiro Typeworks. Wikipedia gives its release as 2005. Microsoft ships it with Windows as "Euphemia", and Apple ships a version called Euphemia UCAS. Tiro later reworked and extended the design as Euphemia version 4 (2023).

summary: A bold, compactly spaced Arabic display typeface with lively, pen-like strokes. Suited to headlines and short texts that need personality.
history: Farah was made by Diwan Software (2001 copyright). Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013), when Mac OS X gained about a dozen new Arabic-script fonts.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A slanting, flowing Arabic-script typeface with a calligraphic, Persian flavor. Its name is Arabic for "Persian." Best for display and decorative text.
history: Farisi was made by Diwan Software (2002 copyright). Apple added it in OS X 10.9 Mavericks (2013).

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with OS X Mavericks

summary: A pixel-based (bitmap-only) Chinese font covering more than 20,000 CJK ideographs, with a blocky, screen-pixel look. It is mainly a reference and compatibility font for the Chinese GB 18030 character standard.
history: The font carries a 2002 copyright from NISC, People's Republic of China. It supports GB 18030, the Chinese government's official character-set standard. Wikipedia's list of macOS fonts records it as "NISC GB18030", a bitmap-only font.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A clean, simple Arabic typeface in regular and bold. For years it has been the standard Arabic font on Mac and iPhone, and it reads well on screen.
history: Geeza was designed by Diwan Software, and Fonts In Use dates the family's start to 1992. It has come bundled with Mac OS X since at least 10.3 Panther (2003), and Diwan describes Geeza Pro as the standard Arabic typeface for Mac OS X and iOS.

summary: A typeface for the Grantha script in regular and bold, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. Grantha is a classical South Indian script historically used to write Sanskrit in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
history: Grantha Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2004 copyright). Apple ships it in the same font file as Tamil Sangam MN, and it also covers Tamil characters. Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A traditional Gujarati typeface in regular and bold, with calligraphic stroke contrast and a serif Latin companion. Suitable for Gujarati-language text.
history: Gujarati MT is a Monotype design with a 1996 copyright. The name inside the font file is "Monotype Gujarati".

summary: A Gujarati typeface in regular and bold, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. It gives Gujarati text a clean, modern look.
history: Gujarati Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2009 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A Gurmukhi typeface in regular and bold for writing Punjabi, with moderately contrasted strokes and a humanist Latin companion.
history: Gurmukhi MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran for Murasu Systems (2003 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "MN" family of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts. Fonts In Use notes that the plain MN fonts pair the script with a humanist sans Latin that has some stroke contrast.

summary: A single-weight Gurmukhi typeface for Punjabi, with sturdy, traditional letterforms.
history: Gurmukhi MT is a Monotype design with a 1996 copyright. The name inside the font file is "Monotype Gurmukhi".

summary: A Gurmukhi typeface in regular and bold for Punjabi, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. It gives text a clean, modern look.
history: Gurmukhi Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran for Murasu Systems (2011 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A Simplified Chinese heiti (sans serif, "black type") typeface in Light and Medium, with plain, even strokes. Built for on-screen Chinese text.
history: Heiti SC was made by Changzhou SinoType Technology, with copyright dates of 2000–2007. It first shipped with Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard (2009) as the Chinese system font. It kept that role until OS X 10.11 El Capitan, when PingFang replaced it.

summary: A Traditional Chinese heiti (sans serif) typeface in Light and Medium, with plain, even strokes. Built for on-screen Chinese text as used in Taiwan and Hong Kong.
history: Heiti TC was made by Changzhou SinoType Technology, with copyright dates of 2000–2007. It shipped with Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard (2009) as the Traditional Chinese counterpart to Heiti SC. It served as a Chinese system font until PingFang replaced it in OS X 10.11 El Capitan.

summary: A friendly, rounded Japanese sans serif (maru gothic) with soft stroke ends, for approachable text, signage, and UI.
history: Hiragino is a Japanese type family designed by the Tokyo studio Jiyukobo (founded by Tsutomu Suzuki, Osamu Torinoumi, and Keiichi Katada) and sold by SCREEN Graphic Solutions, formerly Dainippon Screen. Fonts In Use dates Maru Gothic to 2000. Apple bundles one weight, W4, in the ProN version, which follows the JIS X 0213 character standard.
designers: Jiyukobo (Tsutomu Suzuki, Osamu Torinoumi, Keiichi Katada)

links.label: Fonts In Use: Hiragino Maru Gothic

summary: An elegant Japanese serif (mincho) typeface in W3 and W6 weights, with fine horizontals and brush-like terminals. Ideal for books, editorial work, and refined display text.
history: The Hiragino family was designed by Jiyukobo and has been sold by SCREEN Graphic Solutions (formerly Dainippon Screen) since 1993. It is named after the Hiragino district of Kyoto. Hiragino has been built into Mac OS X from its early days; Apple announced in 2000 that Mac OS X would ship with high-quality Japanese fonts. The ProN version follows the JIS X 0213 character standard.
designers: Jiyukobo (Tsutomu Suzuki, Osamu Torinoumi, Keiichi Katada)

summary: A clear, modern Japanese sans serif (kaku gothic) in ten weights, from the hairline W0 to the heavy W9. A versatile workhorse for Japanese interfaces, signage, and text.
history: Hiragino Sans is Apple's name for Hiragino Kaku Gothic, part of the Hiragino family designed by Jiyukobo for SCREEN Graphic Solutions (formerly Dainippon Screen). Fonts In Use dates Kaku Gothic to 1994. Apple bundles the full ten-weight range.
designers: Jiyukobo (Tsutomu Suzuki, Osamu Torinoumi, Keiichi Katada)

links.label: Fonts In Use: Hiragino Kaku Gothic

summary: A Simplified Chinese sans serif in W3 and W6 weights, designed to match the Japanese Hiragino Sans. A clean choice for mainland Chinese text.
history: Hiragino Sans GB is the Simplified Chinese member of the Hiragino family, sold by SCREEN Graphic Solutions, with copyrights from 2007. It supports the GB 18030 character set, and Apple has included it since Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard.

summary: A high-contrast Devanagari typeface with classical proportions in five weights, from Light to Bold. Built for books, magazines, and newspapers in Hindi, Marathi, and Nepali.
history: ITF Devanagari was designed by Satya Rajpurohit at the Indian Type Foundry, which dates its release to 2011. ITF says the family is optimized for legibility at small sizes and that each style contains 847 glyphs. Apple added it in OS X 10.10 Yosemite (2014).

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A version of ITF Devanagari that uses the letter shapes preferred in Marathi, such as the distinctive Marathi forms of ल (la) and श (sha). Same five weights and high-contrast book style.
history: Designed by Satya Rajpurohit at the Indian Type Foundry (2011 copyright), this is a Marathi-localized cut of ITF Devanagari. Apple ships both versions in the same font file.

summary: A Tibetan typeface in regular and bold for writing Tibetan and Dzongkha, with traditional uchen (headline) letterforms.
history: Kailasa comes from the Otani University Shin Buddhist Research Institute in Kyoto (2006 copyright) and was designed by Yoichi Fukuda, Steve Hartwell, and Shojiro Nomura. It first shipped with Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard (2007), together with the Tibetan font Kokonor, when Apple added built-in Unicode Tibetan support.
designers: Yoichi Fukuda, Steve Hartwell & Shojiro Nomura

summary: A Kannada typeface in regular and bold, with moderately contrasted strokes and a humanist Latin companion. For the Kannada language of Karnataka, India.
history: Kannada MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran for Murasu Systems (2009 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "MN" family of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts. Fonts In Use notes that the plain MN fonts pair the script with a humanist sans Latin that has some stroke contrast.

summary: A Kannada typeface in regular and bold, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin. It gives Kannada text a clean, modern look.
history: Kannada Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran (2009 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: An Ethiopic (Ge'ez) typeface for Amharic, Tigrinya, and other languages of Ethiopia and Eritrea. Its Latin companion has slab serif roots, a tall x-height, and narrow proportions.
history: Jérémie Hornus designed the original Kefa in 2006 during the MA Typeface Design program at the University of Reading. Apple has included Kefa since Mac OS X 10.6. Hornus and Gaëtan Baehr at Black[Foundry] later revised it as Kefa III (2022 copyright), the third version of this Apple system font. They redesigned the Ethiopic and extended it to cover Unicode 14.

summary: A Khmer typeface in regular and bold for the Khmer language of Cambodia, with moderately contrasted strokes and a humanist Latin companion.
history: Khmer MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran for Murasu Systems (2010 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "MN" family of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts. Fonts In Use notes that the plain MN fonts pair the script with a humanist sans Latin that has some stroke contrast.

summary: A single-weight Khmer typeface for Cambodian text, with even, low-contrast strokes and a plain sans serif Latin.
history: Khmer Sangam MN was designed by Muthu Nedumaran for Murasu Systems (2010 copyright). Muthu Nedumaran, founder of the Malaysian company Murasu Systems, designed Apple's "Sangam MN" fonts. Fonts In Use describes their Latin as a grotesque-style sans, unlike the more humanist Latin of the plain MN fonts.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A low-contrast, open Bengali sans serif in five weights, from Light to Bold. Suited to apps, signage, editorial work, and subtitles.
history: Kohinoor Bangla was designed by Satya Rajpurohit and Jyotish Sonowal at the Indian Type Foundry between 2009 and 2015, with OpenType production by Liang Hai. It is part of ITF's multiscript Kohinoor superfamily. ITF notes that the fonts were built into products from Apple, Sony, and others before ITF released them for retail sale in 2018.
designers: Satya Rajpurohit, Jyotish Sonowal (Indian Type Foundry)

summary: A low-contrast Devanagari sans serif in five weights, from Light to Bold, for Hindi, Marathi, and Sanskrit. Works in both body text and display sizes, in print and on screen.
history: Kohinoor Devanagari was designed by Satya Rajpurohit at the Indian Type Foundry between 2009 and 2014, with OpenType production by Liang Hai. ITF dates its release to 2010, and it is part of ITF's multiscript Kohinoor superfamily. Apple added it in OS X 10.10 Yosemite (2014).

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A low-contrast Gujarati sans serif with open counters, in five weights from Light to Bold. Works in both body text and display sizes.
history: Satya Rajpurohit developed Kohinoor Gujarati at the Indian Type Foundry from 2009 to 2014, with OpenType production by Liang Hai. ITF dates its release to 2014. It is part of the Kohinoor Multiscript superfamily and covers Parsi Gujarati and Kutchi as well as standard Gujarati.

summary: A low-contrast Telugu sans serif with open letterforms, in five weights from Light to Bold. A workhorse for apps, signage, and editorial text.
history: Kohinoor Telugu was designed by Satya Rajpurohit at the Indian Type Foundry between 2014 and 2015, with OpenType production by Liang Hai. It is part of ITF's Kohinoor superfamily. ITF notes that the fonts were built into products from Apple, Sony, and others before ITF released them for retail sale in 2018.
